## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top MoA is supported over Aurora and other runners-up by several orthogonal quantitative signals visible in the large-nucleus/high-dose wells. A dose index 0 trial would only repeat high dose biology; more informative discriminator needed.

Requested: Request description of phenotype on lowest-index acquired well (dose 0.01 uM replicate 1) comparing DNA, tubulin and actin to DMSO, with direct inspection for condensed mitotic figures/chromosomes and spindle/tubulin organization around microtubule accumulation; DNA damage predicts no structured mitotic arrest figures, Aurora predicts polyploid/endoreplicated nuclei, tubulin poisons predict spindle/ bundled or depolymerized microtubule pattern.

## Unblinding

Compound: **alsterpaullone** (PubChem CID [5005498](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5005498))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

High-dose alsterpaullone gave a striking large-pale-nucleus signal with frac_large_nucleus z=+25.5, nuc_major_axis z=+17.7 and nuc_dna_mean z=-12.4 in 426 cells, persisting at 1 uM with low density, which I read as damage-associated decondensation/senescence and was reinforced by compare_to_reference_atlas returning DNA damage 5/10 versus Aurora 3/10 and Kinase inhibitors 1/10.

That was a phenocopy error: CDK arrest also lowers cell number and produces enlarged nuclei with dilute DNA staining without polyploidy, but I kept Kinase inhibitors at 0.05-0.07 and never tested the alternative. The decisive acquisition mistake was spending budget on only 2 wells, so all four dose_response calls for nuc_dna_mean, nuc_dna_integrated, frac_large_nucleus and cell_area failed for needing at least 3 wells, leaving total-DNA/ploidy versus decondensation untested and forcing reliance on the atlas plurality and intact tubulin/actin in describe_phenotype.

Unblinded literature shows alsterpaullone is a paullone CDK inhibitor rather than a direct DNA damager, explaining the antiproliferative large-nucleus phenotype without mitotic arrest figures or tubulin bundling/loss that correctly argued against Aurora/tubulin poisons but did not distinguish arrest from damage.

What was right:
- Detected dose-associated antiproliferative effect: 426 cells at 30 uM vs 923 cells at 1 uM with microscopist-confirmed lower density vs DMSO.
- Correctly down-weighted Aurora kinase inhibitors and tubulin poisons because mid-dose fields showed intact tubulin/actin without condensed mitotic figures, spindles, bundles or depolymerization.
- Retained Kinase inhibitors as a runner-up hypothesis from the atlas 1/10 hit, keeping the true broad class in the differential.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread nuc_dna_mean z=-12.4 with enlarged nuclei as DNA-damage decondensation/senescence without measuring nuc_dna_integrated dose trend to exclude G1/G2 arrest-related enlargement.
- Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas plurality 5/10 DNA damage over 1/10 Kinase inhibitors, despite microscopist first suggesting Aurora inhibitors then unknown.
- Acquired only 2 wells over 2 doses so dose_response for nuc_dna_mean, nuc_dna_integrated, frac_large_nucleus and cell_area all failed, and had no low-dose well left to test for arrest versus damage when review requested further discrimination.

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose titration with cell-cycle flow cytometry plus phospho-Rb, cyclin levels, EdU incorporation and gamma-H2AX: CDK inhibition predicts G1/G2 arrest with hypophosphorylated Rb and gamma-H2AX-negative enlarged nuclei, versus DNA damage which predicts gamma-H2AX foci and p53/p21 induction.

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [10363974](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10363974/): Discovery and initial characterization of the paullones, a novel class of small-molecule inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinases. *Cancer Res* (1999) — Paullones were discovered as a novel class of small-molecule inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinases.
- PMID [12669310](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12669310/): Alsterpaullone, a novel cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor, induces apoptosis by activation of caspase-9 due to perturbation in mitochondrial membrane potential. *Mol Carcinog* (2003) — Alsterpaullone is a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that induces apoptosis by caspase-9 activation after mitochondrial membrane perturbation.
- PMID [10495356](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10495356/): ATP-site directed inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinases. *Curr Med Chem* (1999) — Cyclin-dependent kinases are inhibited by ATP-site directed small molecules, the class to which paullones belong.
